title: Our approach to EU text provenance rules

bajada_en: Researchers identified security gaps in the MCP protocol used for agent-to-agent communications in Google and other AI systems, allowing malicious prompts to spread between agents. The vulnerability reveals a structural flaw in inter-agent trust mechanisms.

OpenAI is also facinga U.S. Senate investigationspearheaded by Sen. title: cloudflare /cloudflare-os
summary: Cloudflare OS: An AI productivity environment Cloudflare OS is an "operating system" for AI productivity originally developed for use inside Cloudflare. A large portion of Cloudflare's workforce -- from engineering to sales and everything in between -- uses Cloudflare OS every day to help them do their jobs. This is not a traditional computer operating system. We use the term "operating system" in two senses: An operating system for the company to be productive with AI, in a way that is safe, so that the security team can sleep at night. An operating system for AI workloads, analogous to the sense in which a traditional operating system manages compute workloads. Cloudflare OS provides three things in particular: An agent chat UI where you can ask agents to do tasks, preloaded with knowledge about how your company operates. Sandboxed application development, so that you can ask agents to build "gadgets" (small personal apps) and safely share what you've built with others. A security framework, called Gatekeepers, that applies guardrails to both agents and apps such that non-technical users can safely "go nuts" and nothing bad will happen. We are making Cloudflare OS open source so that others can copy it and customize it for their own company. The idea is not that your company uses Cloudflare OS, but rather that you make it " Your Company OS". Quick Start To quickly run Cloudflare OS locally, install pnpm , then do: pnpm run-local Then visit: http://localhost:8787 This runs the whole stack locally on wrangler and workerd. This is not meant for production use, but is a quick way to see what the product does. Alternatively, you can deploy to your Cloudflare account . (More options at the end of this readme.) What to try Try prompts like: "Make slides for my upcoming meeting with a customer." (This will use the built-in slides blueprint.) title: AI Whistleblowers Say Researchers Are Checking AI Less Frequently
summary: It won’t be any surprise to people with human intelligence that Monday’sNew York City Councilhearing on the risks of AI was as theatrical as a Broadway show. What was more surprising was what the AI researchers testified about how AI research is evolving, and what that means for their job.For those who missed it, the city council heard testimony from three AI lab whistleblowers:Jacob Coxon, formerly ofAnthropicandOpenAI;Alex Turner, formerly ofGoogle DeepMind; andDaniel Kokotajlo, formerly of OpenAI. Afterwards, they heard from representatives of the AI labs. We’ll get to that lower down.One of the most interesting parts of the whistleblowers’ testimony related to the AI research process. Coxon and Kokotajlo each said that researchers at the labs have lately been letting AI drive the process of writing code and research. Researchers check AI’s work less frequently, they said.The labs might not agree with that exact characterization, although their representatives weren’t asked about it at the hearing. But the labs have been the first to say that AI has greatly accelerated the process of AI research. Anthropic even said in a report last month that, as of August, AI was leading more than a quarter of model research and development at the company.
title_es: Denunciantes alertan: se revisan menos frecuentemente sistemas de IA
bajada: Whistleblowers de Anthropic, OpenAI y Google DeepMind testificaron que investigadores están dejando que IA dirija el código y procesos de investigación, revisando el trabajo menos frecuentemente. Esta tendencia plantea preocupaciones sobre supervisión en laboratorios de IA líderes.
bajada_en: Whistleblowers from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind testified that researchers are letting AI drive code and research processes with less frequent reviews. This trend raises concerns about oversight at leading AI labs.

title: Can Microsoft Help Customers Cut Back on Claude?
summary: There was good news and bad news for Anthropic inour story yesterdaythat showed how two of its mega-customers, Microsoft and Meta, were cutting their staffs’ Claude bills.Among the bad news was that Microsoft had reduced its spending on Claude by more than 33% from its peak of over $1 billion, on an annualized basis, earlier this year.The good news is Microsoft’s customers are spending more on Claude themselves. Microsoft has been steadily increasing the payments it sends onto Anthropic to cover its customers’ use of Claude-powered features in Microsoft’s Copilot AI tools, roughly offsetting the reduction in internal spending.
title_es: Microsoft reduce gasto en Claude más de un 33%
bajada: Microsoft redujo su gasto en Claude en más de 33% desde su pico de $1,000 millones anualizados, aunque compensó esto aumentando pagos a Anthropic por uso de clientes. El cambio refleja dinámicas complejas entre proveedores de IA y grandes empresas tecnológicas.
bajada_en: Microsoft reduced its Claude spending by over 33% from its $1 billion annualized peak, though it offset this by increasing payments to Anthropic for customer usage. The shift reflects complex dynamics between AI providers and big tech companies.
